{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "PFS endpoint definition inconsistent between sections",
      "quote": "Progression will be based on an independent radiologic assessment of disease response per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Section 2.1.2 states PFS progression is based on 'independent radiologic assessment' while Section 3 states 'blinded independent central review (BICR)'. These terms may imply different review processes, causing ambiguity in endpoint assessment.",
      "fix": "Harmonize terminology across sections, e.g., use 'blinded independent central review (BICR)' consistently."
    },
    {
      "title": "PFS censoring rule may introduce bias",
      "quote": "PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Censoring PFS at start of new anti-cancer therapy is informative if treatment switch is related to prognosis, potentially biasing the treatment effect estimate. The estimand strategy should be clearly justified.",
      "fix": "Consider a treatment policy strategy for intercurrent events or perform sensitivity analyses using alternative censoring rules."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 105 requires both platinum and checkpoint inhibitor without exception for contraindication to both",
      "quote": "Prior treatment must include a platinum-based doublet chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibitor for advanced or metastatic disease, either given as one line of therapy or as individual lines of therapy unless the subject has a medical contraindication to one of the required therapies.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The criterion allows exception for contraindication to 'one of the required therapies' but not both. If a subject has contraindications to both, they are excluded, which may be overly restrictive and lead to enrollment challenges.",
      "fix": "Clarify that contraindication to either or both therapies may be acceptable with medical monitor approval."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO endpoint assessment limited to Week 12 may miss later treatment effects",
      "quote": "Change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The PRO endpoint only evaluates change to Week 12, which may be too short to capture meaningful differences in a chronic disease like NSCLC, especially if treatment benefit emerges later.",
      "fix": "Consider extending PRO assessment to a later time point or include time to deterioration as a secondary endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "No safety monitoring for specific drug class (KRAS inhibitor) mentioned",
      "quote": "Subject incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, treatment-related adverse events, changes in vital signs, and clinical laboratory tests.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoints are generic and do not include monitoring for known or potential toxicities of KRAS G12C inhibitors (e.g., hepatotoxicity, gastrointestinal effects, skin toxicity). The protocol lacks specific safety monitoring guidance for this class.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety monitoring parameters (e.g., liver function tests, dermatologic assessments) and dose modification rules for AMG 510."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 104 allows prior study enrollment but not current central testing details",
      "quote": "Have documentation of KRAS p.G12C mutation confirmed by central testing through the current protocol or have documentation of KRAS p.G12C mutation through Amgen Study 20190294 prior to enrollment.",
      "page": 58,
      "section": "5.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The criterion is ambiguous about what constitutes 'documentation' from the prior study and whether the central testing method is identical, which could lead to variability in eligibility determination.",
      "fix": "Specify the acceptable documentation and ensure the central testing method is consistent across studies."
    },
    {
      "title": "OS endpoint censoring at 'last contact through the analysis trigger date' may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "Overall survival, defined as time from randomization until death from any cause (subjects who do not die will be censored at the date of last contact through the analysis trigger date)",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'analysis trigger date' is not defined in this section, and the censoring rule may be inconsistent with the estimand description in Section 3 which says 'OS will be estimated regardless of subsequent anti-cancer therapy.'",
      "fix": "Define 'analysis trigger date' and ensure censoring rules align with the estimand strategy."
    },
    {
      "title": "No explicit safety monitoring for docetaxel-related toxicities",
      "quote": "To compare the safety and tolerability of AMG 510 versus docetaxel",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "While docetaxel is a standard chemotherapy with known toxicities (e.g., neutropenia, neuropathy), the protocol does not specify additional monitoring for these events beyond general adverse event reporting, which may be insufficient.",
      "fix": "Include specific monitoring for docetaxel-related toxicities (e.g., frequent blood counts, neurological exams) in the safety plan."
    }
  ]
}
